### Baseline dispatch + phases 4/5/6/2 landed (same branch)

- Baseline run `38878871977` dispatched from commit `28ed8952` (instrumentation only) at 09:12Z, `creative-only` intake #158, `inference_provider=opencode-go`, QA repo `WrazyAI/llqa-158-creative-38878871977-1`. It pins its own SHA; later commits do not affect it.
- Evidence reuse (plan phase 5): new `scripts/creative-evidence-cache.mjs` stores per-candidate rendered evidence + judge result keyed on a digest of candidate sources, shared site inputs, render settings, judge model, and a version constant. Managed contrast-correction blocks are stripped before hashing so persisted auto-repairs do not invalidate their own evidence; `.launchloom`, candidate dirs, per-round evidence dirs, and the candidate-derived `selected` directory are excluded from the shared digest; evidence with missing files or failed judges is never reused. The orchestrator enables reuse by default (`CREATIVE_EVIDENCE_REUSE=false` kill-switch) and passes `evidence-cache/` into each bakeoff; on a hit the round restores screenshots into its own evidence dir so repair/gate inputs keep working unchanged. Diversity judging is deliberately NOT cached (always re-evaluated), so a changed member can never inherit an old diversity pass.
- Bounded concurrency (plan phase 4): per-candidate judges are scheduled immediately after that candidate's render and overlap the next candidate's render, bounded by `createTaskLimiter` at 2 workers (env `CREATIVE_JUDGE_CONCURRENCY`, clamped 1-3). The candidate loop now has a post-render pass that merges deferred judge results, writes reusable evidence, then scores; models, reasoning, screenshots, viewports, and candidate count are unchanged.
- Progress-aware repairs (plan phase 6): `blockingFindingsSignature` (sha256 of normalized blocking findings) plus a stagnation guard in `run-rendered-creative-repair.mjs` (`MAX_STAGNANT_REPAIRS = 2`). Repairs that leave the blocking set byte-identical twice mark a candidate stagnated; its remaining budget is not spent, other candidates can still be repaired, and the loop fails with an explicit `Stagnation guard:` error instead of repeating equivalent work. Budget-cap tests now vary blocker text to keep exercising the pure budget path; new tests cover the guard and the deferred-judge wiring.
- Template adherence (plan phase 2): new `scripts/design-adherence-guidance.mjs` reads the retained Apache-2.0 frontend-design review copy from `docs/design-guidance/anthropic/frontend-design/SKILL.md` at runtime (no network fetch; provenance pinned in that directory's README) and pairs it with a binding `TEMPLATE_ADHERENCE_CONTRACT` (preserve structure/section order/mechanics/interactions; adapt copy, brand roles, imagery, responsive composition; prohibit generic substitutions, invented facts, trade-dress copying, and boxed contrast fixes). Both blocks now reach the authoring system prompt and the repair prompt's cached reference context.
- Structural drift detection: `reference-contract-compliance.mjs` now reports a critical `section-order` finding when `data-reference-section` values appear out of the assigned sequence (extra local sections are allowed). Verified against the real acceptance-run candidates (`candidate-a/b/c` from `llqa-158-creative-38620904674-1`): all three already conform and produce zero section findings, so this adds drift detection without retroactively failing conforming work.

## Creative promotion-gate diagnosis (Nifty `s3Sx8Mu2fG`)

- Task: user-requested investigation into why the creative promotion gate rejects candidates. Systematic-debugging process: evidence first, no fixes proposed before root cause. Report: `docs/creative-gate-diagnosis-2026-10-16.md` on `codex/launchloom-creative-gate-investigation` (this exploration was read-only against product code).
- Evidence: all round evidence from the four matched runs (12 candidates, 105 judged draws, ~40 rounds), the 2026-10-01 calibration record, and historical failed runs. Method: parse every `creative-bakeoff.json` for failures, judge audits, dimension scores, majors, and diversity pairs.
- **Primary root cause (proven):** the judge gate is a near-perfect-score conjunction the current judge pipeline cannot produce. In 105/105 draws: `overall` bar 78 exceeded the maximum ever emitted (77); `spatialRhythm` bar 78 vs max 76; `mobileRecomposition` bar 78 vs max 77; zero major findings achieved 0/105 (median 5 majors per draw). Even relaxing every score bar by 20 points leaves 0 combined passes. The 2026-10-01 calibration set the overall bar to the historical maximum and left the dimension bars unchanged despite recording that no candidate ever held all dimensions at once; its promised follow-up review never ran, and six or more later judge-affecting changes moved the ceiling further below the bars.
- **Contributing causes (proven):** (1) contrast audit bail classes - 7,775 of 7,802 unresolved findings are "overlapping non-ancestor paint" (74%) and "filter/blend/opacity" (15%), which are structural audit limitations routed to author repair even though no source edit can change the audit's inability to prove the backdrop; candidates in this class stay invalid regardless of fidelity. (2) Pool attrition - repeated repair rejections left both #134 runs with one renderable candidate, forcing `incomplete-rendered-evidence` diversity. (3) Deterministic hero-height and media-coverage checks failed in nearly every draw, adding further conjuncts.
- Recommendation (requires product approval, nothing changed here): measured recalibration harness setting bars at a discriminating percentile with holdout verification and automatic re-calibration on judge/reference changes; pixel-based resolution for the contrast bail classes; pool protection; and a decision on the below-bar near-miss preview option left open on 2026-10-01.

### Calibration harness results (Task 2) and the layered root-cause refinement

- Harness: `scripts/calibrate-creative-gates.mjs` (run-stratified candidate-group split, nearest-rank percentile bars, strict-pass curve, bounded near-miss search, scalar-shape alternatives, byte-deterministic report). Artifact: `docs/calibration/2026-10-16-creative-gates.json` (105 samples, 4 runs, 12 candidate groups, 0 skipped). 7 tests; `npm run check` clean.
- **Measured layer 1 - strict conjunction impossible:** 0 of 105 draws pass at every percentile 70-98 even allowing up to 3 majors; `zeroMajorSamples: 0/105` (majors median 5). The October bars sat above every observed maximum for `overall` (77 vs 78), `spatialRhythm` (76 vs 78), `mobileRecomposition` (77 vs 78).
- **Measured layer 2 - near-miss by per-dimension margins is also impossible:** every one of the 105 draws misses more than six dimensions and at least one by over 15 points relative to near-max bars; the bounded-misses search hit its ceiling with run rate 0.
- **Measured layer 3 - scalar delivery shapes:** hard-gate-clean + zero critical findings + `overall >= B` yields run rates 1.0 at B=45, 0.75 at B=50, 0.5 at B=55, 0.25 at B>=58. Critical findings are rare (0 in 102/105, 1 in 3), so the binding constraints are hard deterministic failures and the overall score.
- **Measured layer 4 - provable contrast failures freeze the top draws:** of the 13 draws with overall >= 60, only 3 are hard-gate clean; the rest are blocked by provable contrast fails (849 lines). `contrast fail` composition: default 1363 (62 percent), focus 633 (29 percent), hover 207 (9 percent); by kind: text 1185, control/icon/other 1018. The contrast sweep only ever repairs `kind=text, state=default` findings (`planContrastRepairs` repair-eligibility), so focus/hover/control/icon failures are structurally unrepairable by the sweep; the model repair loop has not cleared them either (base134 candidate-a carried the identical 39 failures across all 11 rounds with `repairs=0`). Nine samples are blocked ONLY by non-default-state contrast fails.
- Consequences for the plan: Task 5 (pixel contrast) must also gain state-aware repair or resolution for hover/focus (the pixel sampler already runs per state; the repair eligibility and correction CSS need state-scoped support), and the artifact's scalar alternatives are the evidence base for Task 4's strict-shape decision. Nothing applied to thresholds yet.

### Task 5 landed: pixel-based contrast resolution + state-aware repairs

- `rendered-contrast.mjs`: `resolveRenderedBackdrop` resolves the structural bail classes (overlapping non-ancestor paint, filter/blend/backdrop-filter, partially covering plates, pseudo-element backdrops) from the rendered pixels of the exact hover/focus/default state: glyph paint (or outline) is hidden only for the capture, the element region is screenshotted and decoded via sharp, and the worst-case per-pixel ratio against the effective foreground decides pass/fail. Element opacity and opacity-only filters fold into the effective foreground alpha; unsettled animations and text-clipped paint remain unresolved (a single frame cannot prove them), and any capture/decode/locate failure fails closed. Audit reports carry `pixelResolved` counts.
- `contrast-sweep.mjs`: repairs are state-scoped. Hover failures repair with `:hover` rules, outline and focus failures with `:focus-visible` and `outline-color`. Default-state repairs keep the strict cross-state guard so a static rule can never clobber passing authored hover/focus paint. Deliberate semantic change: mixed-state cases that used to be refused because a static rule would regress another state are now repaired safely inside their state scope.
- Tests: new `rendered-contrast-pixel.test.ts` (4 tests incl. fail-closed missing element and real collected-target selectors); four audit tests updated to the measured contract (previously unresolved cases that the pixels prove are now honest failures, never passes); contrast-sweep planner tests cover the scoped hover/focus rules, the preserved default-state guard, and continued stripping; contrast suites 66, static-homepage/publish/color + repair-loop 91, all green; `npm run check` 0 errors across 375 files.

### Tasks 3 + 6 + 7 landed: severity policy, pool protection, near-miss preview delivery

- `creative-gate-severity.mjs`: `classifyJudgeFinding` (critical always blocks; majors in content-integrity/accessibility block; fidelity majors are open) and `nearMissAssessment` (hard failures clean, no critical findings, overall >= scalar bar, every rendered dimension above an absolute floor; design findings travel as open findings). Injected defaults `{overallBar: 50, dimensionFloor: 40}` pending Task 4's measured recalibration.
- Pool protection: repair-contract exhaustion now marks a candidate `repairBlocked` instead of excluding it. Blocked candidates keep rendering, judging, and contributing diversity evidence; the bakeoff gained `unselectableCandidateIds` so they can never win the selection while remaining fully evaluated. The gate path stops with an explicit blocked failure instead of re-attempting rejected repairs every round.
- Near-miss preview path (option 4): when the strict conjunction cannot be met, the orchestrator picks the best eligible candidate (highest overall, fewest open findings), runs the visual gate on it (verdict pass/revise, zero criticals required), promotes it preview-only with `selectionMode: "creative-near-miss"`, writes `final/creative-bakeoff.json` with the near-miss selection for downstream stages, and records `summary.status: "previewed-with-open-findings"` with a bounded `nearMiss` block (candidate, overall, bars, gate verdict, open findings). Production promotion never takes this path; `CREATIVE_NEAR_MISS_PREVIEW=false` disables it. The pipeline harness accepts near-miss summaries for preview profiles and its select stage prefers the near-miss candidate by name.
- Switches added to both workflows: `CREATIVE_NEAR_MISS_PREVIEW` and `CREATIVE_PIXEL_CONTRAST` (defaults true; repository variables can disable each).
- Tests: severity suite 37 (incl. judge-finding table and assessment boundaries); orchestrator suite 61 (near-miss delivery, hard-gate refusal, kill-switch, promote-mode refusal, pool-protection walk across five candidates, updated exclusion semantics); pipeline-runner suite 49; `npm run check` 0 errors across 375 files.

### Pixel pass hardening: scoping, occlusion detection, contract migration (same day)

- Scope-marked resolution: hover/focus/menu/detail states resolve only the interacted control subtree (`data-ll-contrast-scope` markers); the default state does the page-wide pass. This removes the repeated page-wide work that pushed unrelated suites over their timeouts under full-suite parallelism (creative-promotion standalone fell back into budget; quick suites green standalone).
- Occlusion detection: hidden-glyph captures were compared with paint-intact captures; identical results (occluded or same-color text) are a measured failure instead of a false pass, which the DOM overlay analysis would previously have flagged. A shadow-veiled input value and covered navigation now fail honestly; genuinely visible text still measures normally.
- `rendered-contrast-paint.test.ts` expectations migrated to the measured contract (24 tests): geometry intent kept in `issues`, statuses now reflect rendered reality (fail for overlapping/occluded/veiled, pass for provable-on-screen cases like the transformed-owner decoration and equal-z document order).

### Field runs 38960348319/38960353832 triage and repair-capability fixes

- Runs completed (~89 min each, 40% faster than baseline) but failed: the near-miss path refused because every terminal candidate still carried hard failures, and a select-stage regression (`nearMissCandidateId` declared inside the `if (!selected)` scope, used outside) broke the fallback selection before the creative stage even mattered. Root data from the field evidence: pixel resolution honestly converts bail-class paint into failures (`(555) 555-0142` 3.970 vs solid #c8ec58; form labels 1.193 to 2.748 over decorations; invisible focus indicators at 1.000 to 1.006), and the sweep could not repair any of them because pixel-resolved findings/peers carry `background: null` and absent outlines are not a color problem.
- Fixes: (1) the select-stage declarations hoisted and the preference extracted into exported, tested `nearMissCandidateId`; (2) `resolveRenderedBackdrop` now records `pixelBackdrop` (darkest and lightest sampled backdrop colors); (3) `planContrastRepairs` proves corrections against every measured backdrop of every state of the selector (DOM backgrounds and pixel extremes alike), refuses unprovable ranges, keeps the cross-state foreground guard, and synthesizes visible focus indicators (`:focus-visible` + `outline:2px solid`) for missing or unreadable rings; pure black/white end candidates make single-sided photo ranges provable while a full black-to-white range at 5:1 is refused; (4) indicator rules stay strippable (`{outline:2px solid #` signature).
- Bakeoff provenance confirmed during triage: `hero exceeds desktop viewport` and `horizontal overflow` are the bakeoff's own hard gates (`hardFailures()`), so the classifier staying conservative on them is correct; `rendered composition:` lines remain open.
- Tests: contrast-sweep 16 (pixel-backdrop proofs, scoped hover proofs, refusal on unprovable ranges, indicator synthesis and stripping), pixel suite 4 with `pixelBackdrop` assertions, pipeline-runner 51 (near-miss preference helper), repair orchestrator 61; `npm run check` 0 errors.

### Field-evidence reproduction and contrast repair fidelity loop (2026-10-17)

- Reproduced the field's persistent contrast failures against the pristine QA clone with the real Astro build (astro build ~2s, so the whole sweep is testable end-to-end locally). Root causes found and fixed, each in the sweep/resolver:
  - Focus indicators are clipped by rounded/overflow-hidden card ancestors; synthesized rings now paint inset (`outline-offset:-2px`) so they render, and the ring's proof region matches exactly that band.
  - The pixel capture now hides all descendant glyph paint during sampling: a child gray label had been sampled as "backdrop" and made every ring color look unprovable.
  - Ring proof uses a computed feasible luminance window (exact, binary-searched over all sampled band pixels; a coarse scan that skipped sparse dark pixels made earlier windows wrong).
  - Failing DOM-proven outline targets now always gather band evidence (previously only unresolved targets were measured), so repairs are proven against every surface along the ring.
  - Repairs accumulated across passes are deduped last-wins per selector and state scope: a stale color from an earlier pass could win the cascade by source order and re-break a fixed element.
  - With pixel evidence but no feasible window, only colors outside the measured luminance range may be planned; interior guesses via extremes are refused. Remaining holdouts (rings crossing multi-tone AA bands, e.g. dark card + lime accent + ivory page) are genuinely unprovable by one static color and stay hard findings for authored repair.
- Evidence: contrast battery 108 tests green; the reproduction drove `enforceBuiltContrast` on the real candidate from 44 findings to 15 (`after`), with the held-out six being the unprovable rings above; the whole run's preview delivery path is independent of these (diagnostic select fallback).


### Field runs 39016571864/81239/83926: sweep budget and provider-outage resilience

- The three runs delivered previews (select fallback + deploy work) but the creative stage failed on two compounding causes found in the evidence:
  1. Repair calls died on **OpenRouter 402 (insufficient credits)**: every repair attempt in these runs failed on billing, and the 402 error propagated as fatal, aborting the loop even when a sibling candidate was already contrast-clean (recal158d candidate-c: zero fails). The orchestrator now treats provider billing/outage errors (402/429/4xx/5xx from the repair provider) as a per-candidate blocked repair, records `status: "blocked"` evidence, and lets the loop reach its terminal paths where a hard-clean sibling can still deliver. Exported behavior covered by a new orchestrator test.
  2. The contrast sweep refused wholesale when a candidate needed more than 32 corrections: recal158d candidate-a showed `repairs: 0` against 213 findings (budget refusal), keeping 141 hard contrast failures. The planner now applies a bounded worst-first plan (default 256 groups / 256 KiB of corrections, matching the writer's cap) instead of refusing: the same candidate went 213 -> 86 findings with 127 repairs in the first validation pass.
- The QA evidence also confirmed the sweep is honest under truncation: remaining findings stay hard; nothing passes unchecked.
- `npm run check` 0 errors; contrast-sweep 16 tests (over-budget contract updated to bounded worst-first), orchestrator 62.

### Field run 39027588170: Go lane proven, rejection starvation fixed (2026-10-17)

- The migrated creative lane worked in production: `repair-usage.json` records `provider: "opencode-go"` with real usage (48k/13k tokens, ~109s per repair) and many repairs completed (`status: "repaired"`). Preview delivered again.
- The run still failed near the finish line because candidate-b (overall 61, every dimension above floor, only two hard failures: hero-fit at desktop and compact) was permanently blocked after three contract rejections, while worse candidates kept consuming rounds; the rejected attempts carried no context into later attempts. Root cause found in the round evidence and closed:
  - Rejection exhaustion now blocks with a two-round cooldown and allows a second rejection cycle before permanent blocking; the candidate re-enters selection eligibility when its cooldown passes.
  - Each retry carries an explicit `repair-output-rejected` finding with the previous rejection reason, and the stagnation guard no longer vetoes that changed attempt.
  - Provider billing/outage blocks are permanent for the run (retrying a downed provider every cooldown starved the near-miss path) and never consume rejection cycles.
  - The no-target path waits out pending cooldowns (bounded by maxRounds) instead of giving up while a near-clean candidate still has retries.
  - Focused-run job timeout raised from 150 to 210 minutes: with repairs succeeding on Go the loop legitimately runs longer (the previous 153-minute run was cancelled by the old limit).
- Tests: orchestrator 63 (new rejection-cooldown/context test, walk updated to the cooldown semantics), full battery re-running before dispatch.
